userStories.description: Pure types + storage + tests; no caller integration in this story. (a) New migration v15 (or next available — verify with grep) `addAgentNotes` in `internal/db/migrations/migrations.go` registered slice AND mirrored in `currentSchemaSQL`. Schema: `conversation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`. (b) New package `internal/agentnote/` with `Store` struct + 4 methods: `Get(ctx, conversationID string) (content string, exists bool, err error)`, `Set(ctx, conversationID, content string) error` (uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE content=excluded.content, updated_at=excluded.updated_at), `Append(ctx, conversationID, line string) error` (read+modify+write under transaction; if note empty, content=line; else content=existing + '\n' + line), `Clear(ctx, conversationID string) error` (delete row). (c) Tests in `internal/agentnote/store_test.go`: 5 cases — Get empty returns ('', false, nil); Set then Get returns content; Append on empty creates; Append on existing concatenates with newline; Clear deletes. (d) NO consumer wiring: do not touch agent loop, system_prompt, channels, api in this story.

userStories.title: Add agent_note LLM tool (set / append / get / clear actions)
userStories.description:
Wire agent_note as an LLM-callable tool with action-dispatch schema (mirroring Phase-L oneOf pattern). (a) New file `internal/agent/tools/registry/agent_note.go` with `AgentNoteTool` struct + Definition + Execute. Schema uses ActionDispatchOneOf helper (Phase-L pattern from action_error.go): action enum [set|append|get|clear]; set requires content; append requires line; get and clear have no extra required params. Description copy: 'A per-conversation scratchpad for your own working memory (todo list, intermediate findings, plan). Use set to replace, append to add a new line, get to read, clear to delete. The note is scoped to the current conversation and garbage-collected at conversation end. NOT visible to the user; NOT promoted to wiki or user memory.' (b) The tool needs the current conversation_id at Execute time. Inject it via a constructor parameter `conversationIDProvider func(ctx context.Context) (string, error)` — the caller (agent loop) provides the resolver. (c) Execute calls agentnote.Store.{Get,Set,Append,Clear} as dispatched. Output format: action=set returns 'ok (N chars)'; action=append returns 'ok (note now N chars, M lines)'; action=get returns the full content as fenced markdown ('
```
<content>
```
'); action=clear returns 'cleared'. (d) Description includes 'REQUIRED PARAMETERS BY ACTION' header following Phase-L convention. (e) Register in `internal/agent/tools/registry/registry.go` alongside search_memory, recall_operational, recall_user_memory. (f) Tests `internal/agent/tools/registry/agent_note_test.go`: 6 cases — set creates note; append on empty creates; append on existing appends; get returns content; clear deletes; sequential set + append + get + clear roundtrip.

userStories.title: Wire agent_note into agent loop + system prompt injection + GC on conversation end
userStories.description:
Make agent_note LIVE in the agent loop. (a) Locate the conversation-id resolver at runtime — verify via grep on `conversation_id` or `ConversationID` in internal/agent/ and internal/channels/. The hub or agent loop knows the current conversation context. Wire the AgentNoteTool constructor with a closure that reads it from the agent invocation context. (b) System prompt injection: in `internal/conversation/system_prompt.go` (or equivalent — locate via grep `prompt_modules` and `base,runtime`), add a new module 'agent_note' that reads agentnote.Store.Get(currentConvID) and injects content if non-empty. Format: '

## Your current note (working memory)

<content>
'. If empty or row missing, inject nothing (zero overhead). (c) GC on conversation end: locate the conversation-close path (likely in internal/conversation/ or a hub event handler — check chat.EventDone or similar). Add a hook that calls agentnote.Store.Clear(conversationID) when the conversation ends or thread is closed. (d) NO change to the agent loop iteration count or system prompt cache key (the note content goes BEFORE 'history' per the cache discipline §3 D13 from master plan — append-only relative to current run, but per-conversation persistent across runs). (e) Tests: `internal/conversation/system_prompt_test.go` extend with agent_note injection case (with content + without); integration test (place in existing chat_test.go or new file) that confirms set->next-run sees note in prompt->clear on done event. Existing tests stay green.
